task.description: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate (WF-02 Step 3b) on REQ-160's test suite. TEST-DESIGNER ran 7 mutation tests (commit 29a3564) against lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex, found 2 real gaps (capability-gate-precedes-body ordering; LuaNumberMarshalling call-site verification via structural test since from_lua/to_lua are literal identity functions), closed both, landing at 85 passing tests. Verify this claim independently -- do not trust TEST-DESIGNER's self-report. Re-run at least 2 of the 7 claimed mutations yourself against the real code to confirm the new tests actually catch them, and re-run mix test to confirm the final state is genuinely green.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-160's 8 real acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml) maps to at least one runnable test -- verified by reading the test file, not the spec's claim about itself.

Independently re-apply at least 2 of TEST-DESIGNER's 7 claimed mutations (recommend: mutation 4, the capability-gate-ordering one, since it's the most subtle; and mutation 6, the LuaNumberMarshalling structural test, since behavioral detection is impossible by construction) and confirm the new tests genuinely fail against the mutated code and pass against the real code.
No skipped, pending, or excluded tests anywhere in test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs for REQ-160 coverage.

Test fixtures are isolated and self-sufficient -- no cross-test state leakage via the process dictionary (particularly relevant here since write_variable/take_staged_writes/0 use process-dictionary state) or shared mutable application env (ServiceCaller resolution).
The zero-Repo-calls telemetry-counter mechanism and the SpyServiceCaller double are genuine spies, not tautological assertions -- confirmed by reading their implementation, not just their name.
test/specs/REQ-160.md accurately reflects the final test file state, including the mutation-testing findings table.
mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both independently re-run and confirmed clean, with real output quoted.

result.verdict: FAIL. Cross-checked every planned test case in test/specs/REQ-160.md section by section against the actual test file content.
findings: GAP against AC1 (docs/requirements.yaml REQ-160, criterion 1): AC1's literal text requires the write-discarded-on-failure property to be 'asserted separately for each failure arm: a raised script error, REQ-154's instruction budget, REQ-155's wall-clock kill, and REQ-156's memory limit.' Only the raised-script-error arm has a concrete behavioral test (`a script that writes then raises leaves the buffer un-drained...`, line 1145). No test in platform_test.exs actually drives an instruction-budget exhaustion, a wall-clock Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill), or a max_heap_size memory-limit kill together with a preceding write_variable call -- grep for max_instructions/max_heap_words/brutal_kill/Task.shutdown over the file returns nothing. test/specs/REQ-160.md's own 'Resolution of open items' section substitutes a single structural guard (platform.ex never calls take_staged_writes() itself) for all four arms uniformly, arguing the mechanism is agnostic to *how* the process died. That argument is logically defensible, but REQ-154/155/156 are all status: done (the mechanisms already exist and are testable), and the requirement's own description text singles out this exact concern -- 'The kill arm is the sharp one -- a brutal kill of the execution process must not leave a half-applied write' -- as the substantive risk the AC exists to catch. Substituting an inference for the three harder, explicitly-named failure arms the requirement calls out by name is not the same as a test asserting the outcome for each of them.

GAP against AC2 (criterion 2): AC2 requires 'a test asserts no intermediate state in which only some are applied is observable, proving atomicity rather than merely eventual application.' test/specs/REQ-160.md section 3's third bullet plans exactly this test -- calling Letflow.Engine.VariableMerge.merge/3 directly against the staged-writes map and asserting the single call's return contains all three keys, 'proving atomicity, not merely eventual application.' This planned test does not exist anywhere in platform_test.exs: grep for VariableMerge/merge( over the file finds no matches outside of Map.merge (an unrelated, incidental use in the execution_context/0 test helper and a fixture). Only the 'accumulate, last-write-wins' test (lines 1095-1108) exists, which shows the staged buffer's final content is correct but never exercises the atomicity claim through VariableMerge.merge/3 at all -- the specific mechanism AC2's own text and the design (§2.6) name.

test/specs/REQ-160.md does not accurately reflect the final test file state (this validator's own AC6), independent of the two AC gaps above: (a) section 2's four failure-arm sub-cases are described as planned test cases but only one is implemented, with the shortfall only partially disclosed in a follow-up 'Resolution of open items' paragraph rather than the section itself being corrected; (b) section 3's atomicity-via-VariableMerge.merge/3 test is planned but never implemented, and no 'Resolution of open items' note flags this omission at all -- the spec is silently inaccurate here, not merely optimistic; (c) section 6's second bullet plans a call_service write-direction test where 'the double captures what it received and asserts the Elixir-side types are integer()/float() respectively' -- no such assertion exists (the only call_service marshalling test, lines 1249-1263, checks only the read/response direction via math.type; the write-direction integer/float claim for call_service specifically is unverified by any double-capture assertion, only inferred from the general structural guard test at lines 1639-1668); (d) section 12's second bullet plans a functional two-tenant test proving `emit_event` under two different prefixes writes into the correspondingly different tenant's events table and never the other one -- this cross-tenant isolation test does not exist; only a single-tenant success test (lines 1460-1488) and a source-grep exist, which do satisfy the narrower literal AC7 text but not the spec's own stated (broader) test 12 plan.
instructions_to_test_designer: For AC1: add three concrete behavioral tests exercising write_variable staged inside a script that then (a) exhausts a small, explicitly configured :max_instructions budget (REQ-154), (b) blocks past a small configured wall-clock timeout and is killed via Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill) (REQ-155), and (c) allocates past a small configured :max_heap_words limit (REQ-156) -- mirror whatever fixture/harness pattern REQ-154/155/156's own test suites already use to trigger these kills (they are status: done, so real, runnable mechanisms exist to reuse), then assert (same shape as the existing raised-error test) that the write is never observed via take_staged_writes/0 read from any process other than the one that ran the script, and that the killed process's own buffer is simply gone. The existing structural guard test is good supplementary evidence and should stay, but does not substitute for these three.

For AC2: add the atomicity test test/specs/REQ-160.md section 3's third bullet already specifies -- stage three writes via a successful script, call Letflow.Engine.VariableMerge.merge/3 directly against the map take_staged_writes/0 returns (current variables %{}, no validations), and assert the single call's return is {:ok, new_variables, events} with all three keys present in new_variables, per design §2.6.

Add the missing call_service write-direction marshalling assertion (spec section 6, second bullet): have a double (or a capturing wrapper around FakeServiceCaller) assert directly on the Elixir-side types (is_integer/1, is_float/1) of the payload it received for an integer-valued and a whole-number-float-valued argument, rather than relying solely on the general structural guard test.

Either implement the cross-tenant emit_event isolation test test/specs/REQ-160.md section 12's second bullet plans, or correct that section of the spec to state plainly that only the narrower literal AC7 (no Repo call with a script-derived prefix, confirmed by grep + single-tenant success) is covered, and that the broader two-tenant functional isolation check was descoped -- with a reason, the same way the mutation-testing section discloses trade-offs. Do the same correction for section 2 (state plainly which of the four failure arms are actually implemented vs. inferred) rather than leaving the section's headline text implying all four are directly tested.

Once these are added, re-run the full mutation-testing pass is not required again (the two independently re-verified mutations already hold), but re-confirm mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs and mix compile --warnings-as-errors are still clean with the new tests added, and update the mutation-testing findings table's 'Net result' section and test count if the new tests change it.
